blocks.html: B2C (Business-to-Consumer) refers to transactions where a company sells products or services directly to individual consumers for personal use. These interactions are typically characterized by shorter sales cycles, mass-market appeal, and decisions driven by factors such as price, convenience, and brand perception.

B2C is one of the most common business models, spanning industries like retail, e-commerce, entertainment, and hospitality. Unlike B2B, where decisions are rational and multi-layered, B2C purchasing behaviour is often more emotional, impulsive, and influenced by marketing, branding, and customer experience.
B2C transactions generally follow a faster and more streamlined journey:

items.title: Awareness
items.html: Consumers discover products through ads, social media, or search.

items.title: Consideration
items.html: They compare options based on price, reviews, and brand reputation.

items.title: Decision
items.html: A quick purchase decision is made, often with minimal stakeholders.

items.title: Purchase
items.html: Transactions happen via online platforms, retail stores, or mobile apps.

items.title: Post-Purchase Experience
items.html: Customer satisfaction, support, and reviews influence repeat purchases.
Shorter Sales Cycles: Decisions are made quickly, sometimes instantly.
Broad Audience Targeting: Businesses market to large and diverse consumer segments.
Emotion-Driven Decisions: Branding, offers, and convenience play a major role.
Lower Transaction Value: Individual purchases are typically smaller compared to B2B deals.
High Volume Sales: Revenue is driven by scale rather than individual deal size.

blocks.html: Quick conversions lead to immediate cash flow.
Ability to reach millions of consumers through digital channels.
Strong branding can create loyal customer bases.
Consumer behavior insights help refine targeting and campaigns.

An e-commerce company selling fashion apparel directly to customers through its website or mobile app operates on a B2C model. Consumers browse products, read reviews, and make purchases within minutes, often influenced by discounts, trends, and brand image.

B2C focuses on delivering convenient, engaging, and value-driven experiences directly to consumers. Success in this model depends on strong branding, seamless customer journeys, and the ability to scale marketing efforts effectively.
